campaigns.title: The Grimmer Debt
campaigns.intro: The Reach is strangling. Commodore Silas Grimmer, once the Admiralty's finest, now sells safe passage to the highest bidder and sinks the rest. Honest trade is dying. You have a small ship, a smaller purse, and a reputation still to make.
campaigns.ending_text: Commodore Grimmer is beaten and the trade lanes are open again. Your name will be toasted in every tavern from Saltmere to Tidewell.

steps.text: Captain {captain}! The Reach needs captains who can turn a profit without turning pirate. Carry this letter to the governor of {p1}. And bring a cargo of sugar: an empty hold makes a poor impression.
Find your feet as a trader: reach a net worth of 4,000.
Carry the sealed letter to the governor of {p1}, with 10 Cane Sugar in the hold.
Load 10 Cane Sugar.
Deliver the letter to the governor of {p1}.
A letter of credit from my old colleague, and a trader who keeps their word. Here is your fee, and a word of warning: Grimmer's raiders are growing bolder.
Letter delivered. Spice traders now deal with you.
Your mother kept the best books in the Reach, Captain. Keep yours half as well and we'll talk again.
Open an account in your own name: keep 3,000 in a bank.
The banker in Puerto Ambar has asked to see you about your family's accounts.
Captain Vega. Your father's creditors have been patient for three years, and patience is expensive. The family warehouse goes to auction at the end of next year unless someone buys it back.
House Vega's warehouse goes to auction unless you buy it back.
Rebuild the family trade: reach a net worth of 12,000.
The barkeep in {p2} hears everything that floats. Find out who is feeding Grimmer his targets.
Talk to the barkeep in {p2}.
Grimmer's eyes are everywhere, love. Merchants who fight back get left alone. Sink one of his raiders and the word gets round.
Win a sea battle against a raider.
Saw your fight from the yardarm. If you want the Admiralty on your side, they need to see coin as well as cannon. Put some savings in a bank.
Hold 10,000 in any bank.
The Admiralty takes note. Musket contracts are open to you.
Your family's ships? The Swallow, the Lantern and the Good Measure. Their crews' families live in {p9}. They say the raiders flew a black pennant with a white gull. Grimmer's colours.
steps.ok: Then I owe those families a visit.

steps.text: The Swallow's bosun drinks here. He says Grimmer's ships always come out of the south on a falling tide. Test it, and you'll know he's not lying.
Win a fight against Grimmer's raiders.
Bring 30 Salt Fish to the crews' families in {p9}.

Fish from a Vega ship. My husband sailed on the Swallow. ... A deserter from Grimmer's deck came through last year asking about the Lark. Moreno, he called himself. He said the Admiralty has a lieutenant who listens.
steps.ok: I know Moreno. He armed my ship.

steps.text: Captain {captain}. Dimas Crowe, of Crowe & Daughters. You have been selling under my prices. In the Reach we call that rude. Stay out of {p5}, and we'll stay friends.
Dimas Crowe warned you away from {p5}. Naturally, you are going there.
Break Crowe's grip: bring 20 Spice to {p5}.
Spice at an honest price! Crowe has been squeezing us for years. They say his books are kept by a clerk who drinks in {p6}.
steps.ok: Then I'll buy the clerk a drink.

steps.text: Find Crowe's clerk in the tavern at {p6}.
The clerk? Passed out in the corner, love. Left this behind. Looks like somebody's second set of books.
Grow your net worth to 45,000 while Crowe's prices collapse.
You've made your point, captain. Grimmer paid me to keep the honest traders poor. I'm done with him. Ask the Admiralty about the fort at Mangrove Key.
Crowe confessed that Grimmer bankrolled his price-fixing.
That ledger you took off the clerk. My cousin keeps books at the bank in {p10}. She'll read it for you, if you're the kind of customer banks like.
Keep 25,000 in a bank so the bankers will read Crowe's ledger with you.
Read Crowe's ledger with the banker in {p10}.

Payments from a commodore's agent every quarter. Payments out to raider captains. And insurance bought on every ship Crowe's rivals lost, from a house called Harrow & Sons. Someone always profits twice in these books.
steps.ok: Harrow & Sons. I'll remember the name.

steps.text: Grimmer's scouts follow Moreno everywhere. Sink 2 of them.
Rafe Moreno has sent word he's in {p11}. Meet him at the tavern.

Captain Vega. You found my muskets useful, I hear. Listen. Grimmer moves his anchorage every season, and only his chart-maker knows where. The chart-maker's sister builds boats. If she comes to you for help, help her.
steps.name: Rafe Moreno

steps.text: Prepare for whatever comes: reach a net worth of 60,000.
A shipwright in {p3} came begging for help. Something about a kidnapping. Go and hear her out.
Visit the shipwright in {p3}.
They took my brother. He drew the only true chart of Grimmer's anchorage. A pirate brig is holding him off {p4}. Bring him home and the chart is yours.
Defeat the pirate brig waiting off {p4}.
Your passenger has been scribbling all night. He says Grimmer's lair is at Blackwater Cay, and that the Commodore sails a stolen Admiralty frigate.
steps.ok: Then we'll need a bigger ship.

steps.text: Grimmer hides at Blackwater Cay. Every fine good is now open to trade.

Grimmer kept me drawing for two years. Coves, reefs, depths. He anchors in a different cove every season, but he always comes back to Blackwater Cay to pay his crews. And he's built a fort at Mangrove Key to guard the lagoon.
steps.ok: Then we'll start with the fort.
steps.name: The Rescued Cartographer

steps.text: A fort won't fall to one sloop. Buy a second ship.
Arm your ships: reach a net worth of 85,000.
The auction is in the spring, Captain. The creditors will take a fair price before then, and not a coin less.
The creditors want proof you can earn: complete a governor contract.
Buy back House Vega's warehouse: keep 60,000 in a bank.
House Vega's warehouse is yours again.
Lieutenant Ada Hale, Admiralty. Grimmer's men hold the old fort at Mangrove Key. Before I commit the fleet I need proof you can fight. Sink three of his raiders.
Sink 3 raider ships for Lieutenant Hale.
Good shooting. The fort's guns cover the whole lagoon. Hit it with everything you have, and bring powder kegs if you can afford them.
Silence the pirate fort at Mangrove Key.
The lagoon is ours. Take this warrant. Report to the governor of {p7}; they have news of Grimmer.
Report to the governor of {p7}.
The Mangrove fort has fallen. The Admiralty is watching you closely now.
With that warrant, governors will give you Admiralty work. Take it. Grimmer will notice a merchant who has friends.
steps.name: Lieutenant Ada Hale

steps.text: Complete 3 governor contracts under the Admiralty warrant.
Reach a net worth of 120,000.
Grimmer's captains signal each other with flags. A smuggler named Nell Varga claims to have his signal book. She wants tobacco, delivered to Blackwater Cay, no questions asked.
Smuggle 30 Tobacco to Blackwater Cay for Nell Varga.
Prompt, and nobody followed you. I like you, captain. The signal book is with my partner in {p8}. Mind Grimmer's wolves on the way: they know you're coming now.
Win 2 battles against Grimmer's wolves.
Collect the signal book from Varga's partner in {p8}.
With Grimmer's signal book, you'll know his ships' next move.
Captain Vega. Your father was a stubborn man and paid for it. I would hate to see the daughter pay twice. Stop now, and I'll see House Vega's ships sail unmolested for as long as I live.
steps.ok: Then I'll make sure that isn't long.

steps.text: Half the merchants in this port got the same letter, Captain. Most of them signed.
steps.ok: Then I'll buy what they're too scared to carry.

steps.text: Carry what frightened merchants won't: load 10 Muskets.
Grimmer has turned his wolves loose on House Vega. Sink 3 of them.
Pay three crews: reach a net worth of 160,000.
Rafe Moreno is in {p11} with his schooner and twelve pardoned men.
Twelve men who owe Grimmer a ship and a burned crew. We'll sail in your line, Captain, if you'll have us.
steps.name: Rafe Moreno

steps.text: Sail with three ships.
Grimmer's crews eat. A brig called the Provender brings their food and powder every month. She's off {p12} this week. No food, no fight.
The Provender's escorts are on the routes. Sink 2 of them first.
Sink Grimmer's supply brig, the Provender, off {p12}.
Grimmer's supplies are on the bottom. His crews will be hungry by the time you meet them.
Blackwater has an old battery on the point that nobody's manned in years. Give my people muskets and we'll keep Grimmer's boats off the beach while you deal with his frigate.
And bring me a cargo of sugar. Gunners work better with rum in them, whatever the Admiralty says.
steps.ok: Sugar and muskets. Some battle plan.

steps.text: Bring 20 Cane Sugar to Blackwater Cay for the battery's rum.
Bring 15 Muskets to Varga's people at Blackwater Cay.
Reach a net worth of 200,000.
Report your plan to Lieutenant Hale through the governor of {p7}.
Two Admiralty brigs will sail with you, unofficially. Officially, they're on a survey. If you lose, they were never there. If you win, the Admiralty planned it all along.
steps.name: Lieutenant Ada Hale

steps.text: Keep the governors on side: complete 2 more contracts.
Grimmer's frigate, the Undertow, carries fourteen guns and a crew of cutthroats. Gather a fortune for powder and repairs before you face him.
Build a net worth of 300,000.
Defeat Commodore Grimmer at Blackwater Cay.
You... a trader. Beaten by a ledger and a lucky broadside. The Reach will forget you, captain.
steps.ok: The Reach will trade freely. That is enough.

steps.text: Grimmer is defeated. The trade lanes are open.
Governors want order back on the routes: complete 2 contracts.
Lieutenant Hale wants your account of the battle, at the governor's house in {p7}.
Grimmer will hang at Kestrel Bay. I'm told I'm to be promoted for a battle I didn't fight. I owe you a favour, Captain Vega. Call it in whenever you like.
steps.name: Lieutenant Ada Hale

steps.text: Grimmer's last captains won't surrender. Sink 3 of them.
The warehouse is yours, Captain, and every creditor has been paid. All that's missing is a house to go with the name.
Reopen House Vega: keep 150,000 in a bank.
A trading house needs a fleet. Own four ships.
House Vega opens its doors again in Puerto Ambar.

campaigns.title: Bad Powder
campaigns.intro: 1694. Three months ago the frigate Resolute fought raiders off Isla Brasa, and two of her guns burst on the first broadside. Four gunners died. The board blamed her master gunner, Tobias Wren, and put him ashore with a sloop and a discharge paper. Wren knows how a gun bursts. He has seen the powder.
campaigns.ending_text: The board struck out your discharge, and the four families shook your hand on the quay. Silas Grimmer sailed away a commodore. You kept the Hammerhead's manifest in oilskin under your bunk, and you never stopped reading the news from the outer Reach.

steps.text: Your papers, Mister Wren. The board finds the Resolute's guns were overloaded by careless hands. You may trade in the Reach. You may not wear the coat again, and you will not set foot in Driftmoor or Isla Brasa while the families are grieving.
steps.ok: The guns were loaded right. The powder was rotten.

steps.text: Discharged from the Admiralty. The Resolute's spare powder was sold off as salvage.
Find out who bought the Resolute's salvage powder: ask the shipwright at {p1}.
Six casks off the Resolute? I bought them for blasting stumps and never used a pinch. Look at it, it cakes like wet sand. Every lid has the same mark burned in: a hammer over a wave.
Get your trade on its feet: reach a net worth of 6,000.
One more thing, Wren. Abel Strand's widow keeps a chandlery in {p2}. The Admiralty paid her a month's wages and called it settled. I thought you should know.
steps.ok: Abel was my second. I'll see her.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 9,000 so you can help the families.
Bring 20 Salt Fish to Nan Strand's chandlery in {p2}. Her shelves are empty.
You've a nerve, Tobias Wren. Every quay in the Reach says you killed my Abel. ... Fish. You brought fish. Sit down before I change my mind.
steps.ok: Abel said nothing to you about the powder?

steps.text: He said it smelled of vinegar, the week before they sailed. He said he'd told the gunner. That's you. Did you listen?
steps.ok: I listened. Nobody above me did.

steps.text: Kip Wade, the Resolute's powder boy, came out of it with burns on both arms. He drinks in {p3} now. He was in the magazine when the casks came aboard.
steps.ok: Then he saw who brought them.

steps.text: Find Kip Wade at the tavern in {p3}.
Mister Wren! They said you'd be hanged. I saw the casks come down, sir. An officer signed for them at the hatch. Gloves, good coat, never looked at us. I didn't see his face, I'm sorry.
steps.ok: Gloves and a good coat narrows it down. Thank you, Kip.

steps.text: Someone told the raiders you're asking questions. Win a fight against them.
Ask at the Ironreef mill office, by the market, who sold that powder to the Admiralty.
You're the gunner from the Resolute. I write up every cask that leaves this yard. Six of yours came back spoiled in March, and somebody signed them out again in April.
steps.name: Hester Quill, mill clerk

steps.text: I can't hand you Governor Thorne's ledger. I can copy one page by candlelight, if the night watchman sleeps. He sleeps very well on cocoa. Thirty sacks of it.
steps.name: Hester Quill, mill clerk

steps.text: Bring 30 Cocoa Beans to Ironreef for the night watchman.
Here. Six casks returned spoiled, signed out to the Resolute's magazine on the ninth of April. Signed by the officer who passed them: Captain S. Grimmer.
steps.ok: Grimmer. He stood on the quarterdeck while my gunners died.
steps.name: Hester Quill, mill clerk

steps.text: And don't come back here for a while. The watchman talks in his sleep as well.
steps.name: Hester Quill, mill clerk

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 16,000.
One more thing, and then I never met you. The mill belongs to Governor Thorne. If this page turns up in a courtroom with my hand on it, I lose my place. Keep it somewhere safe.
steps.ok: It goes in a bank vault tonight.

steps.text: Rent a strongbox for the page: keep 8,000 in a bank.

Mister Wren. I'm told you've been reading other people's ledgers. The board has closed your case, and I'd hate to see it opened by a man who can't prove a thing. Leave it closed and I'll find you a licence to sell to the Admiralty yards.
steps.ok: I'll keep my own licence, Captain.
steps.name: Captain Silas Grimmer

steps.text: A man with governors' work is harder to sink quietly. Complete a governor contract.
Pity. The Reach is a big sea, Mister Wren, and it has a great many rocks in it. Good day.
steps.name: Captain Silas Grimmer

steps.text: Captain Grimmer offered you a licence to drop the matter. You refused.
Raiders have started following your sloop. Win 2 fights against them.
Take the copied page to the governor of {p4}, who sat on the Resolute's board.

This proves the casks were spoiled when they went aboard. It doesn't prove who carried them. A captain's word against a discharged gunner's is no contest, Wren. Bring me the ship that moved the powder.
A ship hunt costs money. Build a net worth of 25,000.
Powder? It leaves Ironreef every month on brigs with no name painted on the stern. The harbour books in {p5} list every ship that clears. They only open them for captains the governors trust.
Earn the governors' trust: complete 2 governor contracts.
Ask to read the harbour books at the market in {p5}.
Here, captain. Every month, the same brig, the Hammerhead, Ironreef to nowhere in particular. Nobody asks where nowhere is.
steps.ok: The Hammerhead. Now I have a name.

steps.text: I'm done drinking, Mister Wren. Let me sail with you. I can't hold a rammer with these arms, but I can count casks and I know that brig's lines.
The Hammerhead uses two harbours. Buy a second ship so you can watch both.
Kip Wade signs on. Your second ship watches the other harbour.
Keep both ships paid: reach a net worth of 45,000.
Raiders' guns don't misfire, sir. Not one. Ours did. If their powder's the good stuff, it came from somewhere good.
steps.ok: Then we'll take a sample out of their magazines.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 55,000.
Sink 2 raiders and scrape a sample out of their powder rooms.
Admiralty grade, sir. Fine as flour, dry as a sermon. That's the powder that should have been in our magazine.
steps.ok: Somebody swapped it and sold ours to the men who fired on us.

steps.text: Your Hammerhead was seen loading off {p6} last night. Low in the water. Go now and you'll catch her at anchor.
Whoever warned them knew our course a week ago, sir. We should change how we send letters.
steps.ok: From now on, nothing on paper.

steps.text: The Tallow's friends are out. Win a fight.
Catch the brig loading off {p6}.
That's not her, sir! It's a sloop called the Tallow, painted up to look like her. Empty hold, and a crew that knew we were coming.
steps.ok: Someone told them. Someone who reads my letters.

steps.text: The Hammerhead was a decoy. Someone knew you were coming.
Only the board knew your plans. Go back to the governor of {p4}.
My secretary, Felix Dorn, copied every letter you sent me. He left two days ago without his wages. I should have seen it. He drinks, he gambles, and lately he's paid his debts.
steps.ok: Where does a man like that hide?

steps.text: Somewhere with a curio dealer who buys stolen letters, I'd guess. And Wren, if you find him, I want him alive.
Pay informers along the coast: build a net worth of 70,000.
Grimmer's men are looking for Dorn too. Sink 2 of them.
Your informers point to the curio dealer at {p7}. Find Felix Dorn there.
Don't. Please. Captain Grimmer pays me to read the board's letters, that's all. If he knows I talked to you he'll put me over the side himself.
steps.ok: Then tell me where the Hammerhead anchors, and I'll get you out of the Reach.

steps.text: Every month, the same three coves. I wrote them down. Passage money first. Forty casks of sugar will buy me a berth to the mainland.
Load 40 Cane Sugar for Dorn's passage.
Dorn's schedule says {p8} this month, sir. If he lied, he lied well.
The Hammerhead's escorts scatter. Sink 2 of them so none can warn Grimmer.
Catch the powder brig Hammerhead off {p8}.

All right, all right! Captain Grimmer gave us the spoiled casks to put in the Resolute's magazine, and we sold her good powder to the raiders off Isla Brasa. The same raiders she fought. It's all in the manifest.
steps.ok: You'll say that to the board.

steps.text: Captured Joss Pruett and the Hammerhead's manifest.
A brig master in irons will say anything to keep his neck. The board will want more voices, Wren. The men who were there, and the ones who lost them.
steps.ok: Kip saw the casks. Nan heard Abel.

steps.text: Witnesses need safe berths. Keep two ships.
Ask Nan Strand in {p2} to speak before the board.
I'll say it to their faces. Abel told you, you told them, they didn't listen. I've waited three months to say it.
Witnesses need safe passage and wages. Complete 2 more governor contracts to pay for them.
Smuggled wine in a discharged gunner's hold, Mister Wren? The customs men are very interested. So are some friends of mine with guns. You should have taken the licence.
steps.ok: There was never any wine in my hold.
steps.name: Captain Silas Grimmer

steps.text: Grimmer has put a smuggling charge on your name and sent raiders after your ships.
Grimmer's raiders are hunting your ships. Sink 3 of them.
Pay the lawyers fighting the smuggling charge: build a net worth of 120,000.
He offered pensions, sir. The families could use them.
steps.ok: They could. They'll get them from someone who isn't buying silence.

steps.text: Start your own fund for the families: keep 40,000 in a bank.
Governor Thorne of Ironreef has asked to see you. Call at his house.

Mister Wren. My mill made honest powder. What a captain does with it after is the Admiralty's business. Name Pruett, name Grimmer if you must, and leave Ironreef out of it. I'll pay each of the four families a pension from my own purse.
steps.ok: Your mill took spoiled casks back and sold them twice.

steps.text: Sold them once, Mister Wren, to the Admiralty, and the Admiralty sent them back to us. My clerk recorded it properly. Ask her. The pensions stand either way. Good day.
Thorne offered pensions to the four families if Ironreef is kept out of it.
Thorne said to ask his clerk. Find Hester Quill at the Ironreef market.

He's right, as far as it goes. The mill wrote everything down. That's the trouble with writing everything down. If the board asks me, I'll swear to the page. I won't lie for Thorne and I won't lie for you.
steps.name: Hester Quill, mill clerk

steps.text: Grimmer will try to stop you reaching Kestrel Bay. Sail with three ships.
Frigate on the horizon, sir, Admiralty lines and no Admiralty flag. She's waiting off {p9}, right across our course to the board.
steps.ok: Grimmer's last argument. Clear for action.

steps.text: Refit for a frigate fight: build a net worth of 180,000.
Break through the Black Gull off {p9}.
The Black Gull struck her colours. Her captain would not say who sent him. He didn't need to.
Show the board you're a trusted trader: complete 2 contracts.
The board meets at Kestrel Bay next season. Build a net worth of 240,000 so they take a merchant seriously.
Bring the manifest, the page, Quill's affidavit and your witnesses to the board at Kestrel Bay.

The board has read the manifest. Your discharge is struck out and your pension restored, Mister Wren. As for Captain Grimmer, he has friends who outrank everyone in this room. He is to be made commodore and posted to the outer Reach.
I'm moving him where he can't embarrass us. It's the most the Admiralty will do. I'm sorry.
steps.ok: Then I'll keep the manifest. Someone will want it one day.

steps.text: The board also offers you your old rank back, Master Gunner. The coat is on the table.
steps.ok: Give the pension to the four families. I'll keep my sloop.

steps.text: Thorne's pensions never came. Set up a fund for the four families: keep 60,000 in a bank.
Tell Nan Strand in {p2}.
A fund. In Abel's name. ... You're a stubborn old fool, Tobias Wren. Come for supper on Sunday.
Your name is cleared. Grimmer is promoted to commodore. You keep the Hammerhead's manifest.

campaigns.title: The Second Seal
campaigns.intro: 1699. Ines Calder, called Ash, cut customs seals for half the smugglers in the Reach until Saltmere put her name on a gallows notice. This spring her mark started turning up on crates of muskets sold to raiders. She didn't cut those seals.
campaigns.ending_text: Your name came off the musket notices, though Saltmere still wants you for the old seals. Ewan Lisle went to prison and Dimas Crowe went back to buying up markets. You signed half shares with Nell Varga at a table in Blackwater Cay, and neither of you read the contract.

steps.text: There's a new notice on the harbour wall, Ash. Your face, your name, and a fresh charge: customs seals on musket crates bound for raiders. Somebody's using your mark.
steps.ok: My mark's the only honest thing I own.

steps.text: Keep trading while you pay: reach a net worth of 4,000.
Then mind your debts. Half this town would sell you to the Saltmere bailiffs for less than you owe.
Pay off your debt so nobody in Driftmoor has a reason to sell you out.
Paid off the moneylender. Driftmoor will keep its mouth shut, for now.
The Reeve likes you, Ash, and she hates Saltmere. Bring her a cargo of cocoa and she'll like you more.
steps.ok: Bribery by cocoa. My favourite kind.

steps.text: Bring 15 Cocoa Beans to Driftmoor.
Ask the governor of Driftmoor who paid for the notice.
Saltmere's bailiffs paid for it, and Saltmere pays a bounty I don't care to collect. I've no love for Saltmere. Keep your trade clean in my harbour and I'll keep forgetting your face.
Earn enough to travel: reach a net worth of 8,000.
Show the notice to Nell Varga at the tavern in Blackwater Cay.
Sit down. A notice with your face on it. I taught you better than to get famous.
steps.ok: I didn't cut those seals, Nell.

steps.text: I know. You'd have spelled 'customs' right. Bring me twenty sugar for my rum men while I think about who did.
Bring 20 Cane Sugar to Varga at Blackwater Cay.
I need a real crate seal in my hand, not a notice. Raiders carry them. Take one off a raider and bring it here.
Reach a net worth of 12,000.
Win a fight against raiders and take a sealed crate.
Steel die. Look at the edge, clean as a coin. Nobody carves that. Somebody paid a real engraver, and there aren't many in the Reach.
Curio dealers know every engraver alive. Ask the one at {p1}.
Steel dies? Only one man in the Reach ever cut them, old Mattias Fenn, who made the mint's coin stamps. Retired now, drinks in {p2}. His hands shake too much to have done this.
Pay your way along the coast: reach a net worth of 16,000.
Find Mattias Fenn at the tavern in {p2}.
Ash Calder. I've seen your boxwood work. Clumsy, but honest about it. This one isn't mine. I taught a boy last winter, a clerk with good eyes and no money. He bought my old tools on credit.
He never paid the credit. Bring me ten chests of spice for my wife's kitchen and I'll remember it.
Bring 10 Spice Chests to Mattias Fenn in {p2}.
Ewan Lisle. Clerk to some merchant who buys a great deal of everything. Thin, ink to the elbows.
Word came back. A merchant called Dimas Crowe has bought muskets in three ports this season. Crowe & Daughters, he calls his house. He has no daughters. His clerk is a Lisle.
steps.ok: A man who lies on his own signboard.

steps.text: Ask the merchants of {p3} about Crowe's buying.
Crowe pays in good silver and wants receipts in other people's names. His clerk does the writing and sails a sloop called the Second Seal.
steps.ok: The Second Seal. He's laughing at me.

steps.text: Build a war chest: reach a net worth of 30,000.
Muskets cost silver, and silver leaves a trail at the bank. Bankers talk to customers with deep pockets.
Reach a net worth of 45,000.
Keep 15,000 in a bank so the bankers take you seriously.
Ask the banker in {p4} where Crowe's silver goes.
Crowe & Daughters draws silver here every month, and a raider captain collects it. A woman called Ottilie Brack. She signs with a cross and counts every coin twice.
steps.ok: Crowe sells the raiders muskets and pays them too?

steps.text: He pays them to raid his rivals. Then he buys the rivals' markets cheap. I never said any of this.
Brack's raiders carry crates under your seal. Sink 2 of them.
Two more crates with your mark go into Varga's cellar as evidence.
A smuggler with governors' work is harder to hang. Complete 2 governor contracts.
The Second Seal is a fast little sloop. One ship chases, she runs. Two ships, she runs into the other one.
steps.ok: Then I need a second ship.

steps.text: Buy a second ship to cut off the Second Seal.
Arm both ships: reach a net worth of 55,000.
The Second Seal put in at {p5} for water. Her clerk was buying ink by the bottle.
Lisle's lookouts are watching the routes. Sink 2 so he doesn't hear you coming.
Run down Crowe's clerk and the Second Seal off {p5}.
Mister Crowe said it was a joke! Your mark on his crates, the bailiffs chasing you, nobody looking at him. I only cut the die. I swear I only cut the die.
steps.ok: Then you'll swear it to a governor.

steps.text: Captured Ewan Lisle, Crowe's clerk, and the steel die he cut.
Crowe will have me killed before I reach any governor. He has people in every port. Please. Somewhere he can't reach.
steps.ok: There's one port Crowe doesn't own.

steps.text: Crowe's men are hunting Lisle. Sink 2 before they reach Blackwater.
Hide Lisle with Varga at the tavern in Blackwater Cay.
You've brought me a clerk. I asked for sugar. ... Fine. He sleeps in the cellar with your crates. If he steals the rum I'll drown him myself.
Miss Calder. My clerk is a fool, and you're welcome to him. Let's be practical. Twenty thousand in silver, and you forget my name.
Crowe's money is everywhere. Build a net worth of 80,000.
Crowe has paid every raider on the coast to sink your ships.
Crowe's hired raiders come for you. Win 2 fights.
Keep the governors on your side: complete 2 more contracts.
You're the seal-cutter. Crowe says you cost him a clerk and a die. He's paying me double to take them back, and I'd like the money.
Brack never fights where she can't run. Bring three hulls or bring none.
Refit for a brig fight: reach a net worth of 110,000.
Brack's brig, the Whelp, is waiting off {p6}. Beat her.
Brack escaped in a boat, but her cabin held Crowe's receipts in Lisle's hand.
Find a governor who will hear Lisle. Try {p7}.

Saltmere wants you for the old seals, Miss Calder, and Saltmere is a powerful friend to lose. I'll hear your clerk, but I need to know you'll still be trading here next year. Show me a house of real standing.
Build a house of standing: reach a net worth of 130,000.
Bad news, Ash. Customs took Nell Varga at {p8}, with a hold full of tobacco. Someone tipped them off. The bail's steep.
Raise 40,000 in cash for Varga's bail.
Pay Varga's bail at the governor's house in {p8}.
Forty thousand. For an old smuggler with bad knees. You're a worse businesswoman than I taught you to be.
Paid Nell Varga's bail.
Crowe won't stop at me. Get your ships together, all of them, and keep them together until this is done.
Keep the governors close: complete 2 contracts.
Sail with three ships.
Clear Crowe's raiders off the routes: sink 3.
A governor will ask how a clerk learned to cut steel. Your old engraver can answer that better than the clerk can.
Ask Mattias Fenn in {p2} to speak at the hearing.
I'll go. My wife says the spice was the best she's had in years, and a man should pay his debts. Besides, I'd like to see Lisle's face when I tell them his letter 'R' leans left.
Every single one. Bring me eight bolts of fine cloth for a respectable coat, and I'll be there.
steps.ok: Eight bolts. You'll look like a governor.

steps.text: Bring 8 Fine Cloth to Mattias Fenn in {p2}.
The governor wants to see you're settled: complete a contract.
Bring Lisle, the die and Brack's receipts to the governor of {p7}.

The die matches the seals, the receipts match the clerk's hand, and the clerk has confessed. The musket charge against you is dropped. Saltmere's old charges are Saltmere's business. As for Crowe, a clerk's word won't hang a man with that much silver.
steps.ok: He'll trip over his own ledgers one day.

steps.text: The musket charge is dropped. Crowe walks free, for now.
You've cost me a clerk, a die and a captain, Miss Calder. I've hired a galleon to collect what I'm owed. She's called the Gilded Purse. I thought you'd appreciate the joke.
Fit out for a galleon fight: reach a net worth of 200,000.
Sink the Gilded Purse off {p9}.
The Gilded Purse is on the bottom. Crowe has run out of people to send.
Put up your half of the partnership: keep 120,000 in a bank.
Go home to Varga at the tavern in Blackwater Cay.
You could have taken his money. Twice.
Then work for me. Half shares, and you keep your own seals out of my crates.
You and Nell Varga are partners.

campaigns.title: Turncoat
campaigns.intro: 1701. Rafe Moreno was sailing master on Commodore Grimmer's frigate for four years. Last month he watched Grimmer burn a merchant ship, the Lark, with her crew still aboard. That night Moreno took a schooner and twelve men and slipped away. Grimmer wants the schooner back and Moreno on the bottom.
campaigns.ending_text: The Admiralty pardoned you and your twelve men. Brack's Hound was towed into port under a borrowed flag, and the Lark's log went into Lieutenant Hale's strongbox. The next year a merchant captain from Puerto Ambar went after Grimmer herself. You drank to her in every tavern that would still serve you.

steps.text: Grimmer's people were in here last night asking after you, Rafe. I told them you'd drowned. They'll check.
Sell what's in the hold: reach a net worth of 4,000.
Get clear of Blackwater Cay: sail to {p1}.
Twelve of us came with you, captain. Twelve of us borrowed from the Blackwater lender to pay for the quiet. He'll sell us to Grimmer if we don't pay him back.
Grimmer's scouts are on your wake. Win a fight against them.
They were flying Grimmer's pennant and still they hesitated, captain. They know your schooner. Half of them learned to sail on her.
Start trading to pay the crew: reach a net worth of 8,000.
Rebuild your purse after the debt: reach a net worth of 14,000.
Pay off the Blackwater lender before Grimmer outbids you.
Debt's clear. The lads say they'll follow you anywhere now, as long as it isn't back.
Your face is on a poster in every port Grimmer pays for. A cotton trader is the dullest man on any quay. Nobody looks at a cotton trader.
A cotton trader still has to fight raiders. Win a fight.
Sell yourself as a cotton trader: bring 30 Cotton Bales to {p2}.
Nobody on the quay at {p2} looked twice at a cotton trader.
You've been talking in your sleep, captain. About the Lark. There's a woman in {p3} who says she swam from her. Pia Sorel.
steps.ok: Then I owe her a visit.

steps.text: She didn't call the bailiffs, captain. That's something.
Reach a net worth of 18,000.
Find Pia Sorel at the tavern in {p3}.
I know your face. You were on his quarterdeck while we burned. Give me one reason not to call the bailiffs.
steps.ok: Because I want him hanged for it.

steps.text: Two of us got off. Tomas sold the logbook to pay his passage home. I don't know where. Find it, and I might believe you.
Grimmer's raiders know your schooner. Some fire high on purpose.
Win 2 fights against Grimmer's raiders.
Keep the crew fed and armed: reach a net worth of 25,000.
Show Vega what you can carry: bring 20 Cane Sugar to Puerto Ambar.
A merchant heir in Puerto Ambar is asking questions about Grimmer. Find her at the market.
You sailed for him. Grimmer's raiders took three of my family's ships, and our house went under. I want to know why.
steps.ok: Your ships wouldn't pay him for safe passage.

steps.text: Then help me prove it. There's a lieutenant in the Admiralty, Ada Hale, who still reads her letters. Take her this one from me.
Reach a net worth of 35,000.
Bring Vega's letter to Lieutenant Hale at the governor's house in {p4}.
A deserter from Grimmer's own quarterdeck. Give me something I can check, Moreno, and I'll put your name on a pardon. What happened to the Lark?
steps.ok: He burned her. With the crew aboard.

steps.text: I believe you. The Admiralty won't, not on your word. Bring me the Lark's log, or a survivor who'll swear to what she saw.
A sailor called Tomas sold a burned logbook to a curio dealer in {p5}, the lads say. Paid for his passage with it.
The Lark's logbook was sold to the curio dealer at {p5}.
Waterlogged, half the pages gone. I was going to ask a price. Take it. I don't want anything Grimmer's men are looking for.
Grimmer will pay well for that book. Make yourself harder to buy: reach a net worth of 45,000.
Reach a net worth of 55,000.
Grimmer knows you have the log. His wolves are out.
Sink 3 of Grimmer's wolves before they find your crew.
Rafe. We have your bosun. Big man, talks too much about you. Bring me the book, alone, off {p6}, and you can have him back.
steps.ok: I'll come. I won't come alone.
steps.name: Captain Ottilie Brack

steps.text: While you were gone, captain, I counted their guns. Eight on the sloop, and Brack's frigate has twenty.
steps.ok: Then we'll need more than luck.

steps.text: Governors' work buys you friends in port: complete a contract.
Brack's sloop, the Jackal, holds Teo Brandt off {p6}. Take him back.
Took you long enough, captain. Brack wasn't aboard. She left her mate to lose the fight for her. That's how she does it.
Teo Brandt is back aboard. Brack wasn't on the Jackal.
Twelve men on one schooner is one target. Put some of us on a second hull and Grimmer has to choose.
Buy a second ship and split the crew.
Keep both crews paid: reach a net worth of 70,000.
Grimmer's men are watching Pia's town. Sink 2 of them.
Show Pia Sorel in {p3} the Lark's log.

That's the captain's hand. That's the last page he wrote, the night before. ... All right. I'll swear to what I saw from the water. But my mother lost her house when the Lark went down, and I want it back.
Buy back the Sorel house: keep 30,000 in a bank.
Pia Sorel signed her statement before a magistrate.
Your price went up again, Rafe. Ten thousand for you, five for the schooner, and a barrel of rum for every one of your men. Grimmer must be worried.
Bounty hunters are out. Win 2 fights.
Stay ahead of the bounty: reach a net worth of 100,000.
Bring the log and Pia's statement to Lieutenant Hale in {p4}.
The log and a sworn witness. That's a case, Moreno. I'll send it to the Admiralty board. It'll take months, and Grimmer will hear about it in weeks.
Governors who owe you are harder for Grimmer to buy. Complete 3 governor contracts.
One more question. Where does Grimmer anchor? If I'm to go after him one day, I need his chart.
steps.ok: He moves every season. Only his chart-maker knows where.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 130,000.
The chart-maker's sister builds boats in {p7}, captain. She doesn't know what her brother draws for a living.
Warn the shipwright at {p7} about her brother's employer.
My brother draws charts for a commodore. He says it pays well and he can't say more. ... You're telling me it's Grimmer. If anything happens to him, I'll know who to ask for help.
steps.ok: Ask the Admiralty for Lieutenant Hale.

steps.text: You warned the chart-maker's sister. If Grimmer takes her brother, she'll go to Hale.
Rafe. You taught me to sail, so I'll make this quick. Give me the schooner and the book, and Grimmer lets your crew live. Refuse, and I come with the Hound.
steps.ok: You'll have to come and take them.
steps.name: Captain Ottilie Brack

steps.text: You'll need every hull against the Hound. Sail with three ships.
Brack's escorts are gathering. Sink 2 of them.
Reach a net worth of 160,000.
Marisol Vega has sent for you. Find her at the market in Puerto Ambar.
I'm fitting out a sloop. My mother's ledger, my father's name and every coin I could borrow. Lieutenant Hale says you're the man who'd know what a merchant should carry against Grimmer.
steps.ok: Muskets, and the nerve to use them.

steps.text: Bring 10 Muskets to Vega in Puerto Ambar for her new ship.
Thank you, Mister Moreno. If I ever find Grimmer, I'll tell him who armed me.
Refit for the fight: build a net worth of 200,000.
Brack and the Hound are waiting off {p8}.
You always did fight better than you lied, Rafe. Take the Hound. Grimmer won't forgive me for losing her anyway.
steps.name: Captain Ottilie Brack

steps.text: The Hound struck her colours. Brack went over the side in the night and swam for it.
A pardoned man needs honest work: complete 2 contracts.
Bring the Hound's colours to Lieutenant Hale in {p4}.
The Lark's log, a sworn witness and the Hound's colours. That's enough for your pardon, Moreno. It isn't enough for Grimmer. He moves his anchorage every season, and only his chart-maker knows where.
steps.ok: His sister will come to you.

steps.text: Marisol Vega will sail within the year. If she comes to me, I'll know what to tell her.
steps.ok: Tell her the Lark's crew were good people.

steps.text: Pardoned. The Lark's log is with Lieutenant Hale.
Pardoned men, captain. All twelve. The lads are asking what we do now.
steps.ok: We trade, and we pay everyone their share.

steps.text: Pay twelve men their shares: keep 90,000 in a bank.
Tell Pia Sorel in {p3} that her mother's house is hers again.
I didn't think you'd do it. ... There's a berth on your ship for a woman who swims well?

campaigns.title: The Compact
campaigns.intro: 1705. Three years after Grimmer's flagship went down, the Reach is free to trade, as long as it buys its cannon from Ironreef and its water from Tidewell. Governor Magnus Thorne and Governor Liesl Vann call their arrangement the Compact. Hester Quill kept both their ledgers for eleven years. She left with copies, and now neither port will let her ashore.
campaigns.ending_text: Thorne lost his seat and Vann kept hers, at fair prices. Water from your spring sold by the cask, Tobias Wren's powder filled holds from Saltmere to Puerto Ambar, and harbour clerks across the Reach started keeping second copies. You still can't go back to Ironreef. You don't miss the view.

steps.text: Miss Quill. Ironreef and Tidewell have written to every governor in the Reach. You stole private papers, they say. I don't care what you took, but I can't be seen helping you.
Saltmere has always been a fishing town, miss. Fish sells everywhere, even under a Compact.
Load 20 Salt Fish to start your trade.
Build a trade of your own before you take on the Compact: reach a net worth of 8,000.
Ships are leaving the Reach, miss. No cannon without the Compact's stamp, no water without the Compact's price. A captain in {p1} is stuck with a hold of cocoa he can't afford to sail home.
steps.ok: Then I'll buy his cocoa and he can sail light.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 12,000.
Buy 20 Cocoa Beans off the stranded captain's hands.
The stranded captain sailed home light. He promised to tell his friends about you.
Ask the barkeep in {p2} about water that doesn't come from Tidewell.
There's a spring above the town, sweet as anything. The Compact paid the old governor to fence it off. Fences rot, love, and the land is for sale.
Put 12,000 in a bank to buy the spring rights above {p2}.
Bought the fenced spring above {p2}.
Water's no good without casks, love. Every cooper in the Reach buys his staves from Ironreef. Except the shipwright in {p3}, who's too stubborn to buy anything.
Reach a net worth of 18,000.
Bring 20 Hardwood to the shipwright at {p3} for staves.
Hardwood. Real hardwood, not Ironreef's pine painted brown. You'll have your casks in a fortnight, and I'll take payment in water.
Your shipwright wants payment in water and fish. Bring 15 Salt Fish to {p3}.
Your first casks are full. Captains are lining up on the quay at {p2}.
Selling water needs a harbour licence. Earn one by completing a governor contract.
Grow the water trade: reach a net worth of 22,000.
Someone is selling powder outside the Compact in {p4}. Find the seller at the tavern.
Ink on your cuffs. You were the girl in the Ironreef mill office, back in ninety-four. You copied a page for me once.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Then I'll pay now. I cast my own powder these days, outside the Compact. Bring me 30 hardwood for charcoal and I'll fill any hold that asks.
steps.ok: Thirty hardwood. I'll bring an invoice.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Bring 30 Hardwood to Tobias Wren for charcoal.
Tobias Wren sells powder outside the Compact. The Reach has a second source.
First batch is dry. The Compact's thugs know it, too. They'll be waiting on the routes.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Get Wren's powder through: win 2 fights against the Compact's hired raiders.
Reach a net worth of 35,000.

Miss Quill. You kept my books for eleven years, and you kept them well, which is why I know you understand arithmetic. A spring and a gunner are small numbers. The Compact is a large one. Come home. Your desk is waiting.
Thorne's answer comes with guns. Win a fight against his hired raiders.
Thorne wrote, asking you back. You wrote a total at the bottom of his letter and sent it back.
Reach a net worth of 50,000.
Vann measures people in silver. Reach a net worth of 70,000.
Governor Vann has come to {p5} to meet you on neutral ground. Find her at the market.
Thorne writes letters. I prefer to buy things. Thirty-six thousand for your spring, Hester. Three times what you paid. You'll be rich and nobody will chase you.
Everything is for sale. You taught me that, in my own ledgers. Think about it.
The governor of {p6} has sent for you.
The Compact has hired a privateer, Miss Quill. A barque called the Contract, with a letter of marque signed by Thorne himself. She's sinking anyone who buys your water or Wren's powder.
steps.ok: Then she sinks me first, or I sink her.

steps.text: The Contract's escorts are on the routes. Sink 2 raiders.
Fit out for a barque fight: reach a net worth of 80,000.
Sink the privateer Contract off {p7}.
We sailed on orders under Thorne's seal. Here, take them. I'm not drowning for an ironmonger.
steps.ok: I'll take the orders. Thank you.

steps.text: The Contract is sunk. Her mate gave you Thorne's orders.
You want to hurt the Compact? Don't chase Thorne. Chase his payroll. Three governors take a salary from the Ironreef mill, paid through the bank in {p8}.
steps.ok: A payroll. Now that's a ledger I'd like to read.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 95,000.
Bankers open their books for big depositors. Keep 40,000 in a bank.
Ask the banker in {p8} about the Ironreef mill's payments.
Three governors, paid on the first of every month. I copied the list because nobody told me not to. You clerks are a dangerous breed.
Your spring fills more casks than your sloop can carry, Quill. Get a second hull, and I'll paint 'Free Water' on her side myself.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Buy a second ship for the water trade.
Supply governors with free water: complete 2 governor contracts.
Reach a net worth of 110,000.
The governor of {p6} is on the salary list. Ask about it.
You warned me about the Contract, and all the while I was on the same payroll as the man who hired her. I didn't think of it as a bribe, Miss Quill. I thought of it as a retainer.
No. They don't. I'll stop taking it, and I'll say so when the books are read. Bring me a cargo of muskets for the harbour guard, so nobody says I sold my town's safety too.
Bring 12 Muskets to the governor of {p6}.
Thorne's bought a frigate. Navy lines, twenty-two guns, and he's named her the Anvil. He means it as a joke. It isn't a funny one.
steps.ok: Then we'll need more than two hulls.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Sail with three ships.
Clear the Compact's escorts from the routes: sink 3.
Harbour clerks keep every port's books. Meet the clerks at the market in {p9}.
Five of us came, miss, from five ports. We've all seen Compact money in our books. Nobody ever asked us about it. You're asking.
steps.ok: Keep a second copy of everything. Bring it to me.

steps.text: Clerks from five ports have started keeping second copies.
Reach a net worth of 160,000.
You're trusting Vann? She sold you water at three prices for eleven years.
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Keep the governors listening: complete 2 contracts.
Governor Vann has asked to meet again in {p5}.

Thorne bought a frigate without asking me. Thorne pays three governors I didn't know about. I can do arithmetic too, Hester. Leave my wells to me, at fair prices, and I'll say all of it before any governor you like.
Liesl Vann will testify against Thorne, if Tidewell keeps its wells at fair prices.
Fit out for the Anvil: reach a net worth of 220,000.
The Anvil is waiting off {p10}. Sink her.
The Anvil is on the bottom. Thorne has no more ships to buy.
The governors will only hear a trader of standing. Build a net worth of 280,000.
Lay the ledgers, Thorne's orders and the salary list before the governor of {p11}.

Water sold at three prices. A privateer paid out of a foundry's accounts. Three governors' salaries topped up by a mill. These will be read aloud in every harbour in the Reach, Miss Quill. The Compact is finished.
steps.ok: Read the totals slowly. People like totals.

steps.text: The Compact's ledgers are read in every port.
Reach a net worth of 320,000.
Bring Tobias Wren his share in {p4}.
Eleven years late, and you brought an invoice. 'One page, copied by candlelight, at risk of employment.' What's the total?
steps.name: Tobias Wren

steps.text: Keep the free trade going: complete 2 more governor contracts.
The clerks want a guild, miss. A room, a strongbox, and someone who knows how to keep two copies of everything. They want you.
steps.ok: Then I'll need a very large strongbox.

steps.text: The guild needs ships to carry its copies. Own four ships.
Found the Clerks' Guild: keep 100,000 in a bank.
The Clerks' Guild opens its doors, with two copies of everything.

campaigns.title: The False Light
campaigns.intro: 1708. Twenty years ago Okoro Bale was a young navigator on the Morning Star when she struck the rocks below Lanterna on a clear, calm night. The lighthouse was dark. Eleven men drowned, and Bale swore he would never see that harbour again. Now ships are going down on clear nights all over the Reach.
campaigns.ending_text: Lanterna lit its lamp under a new keeper and read out the names of the Morning Star's eleven. You weren't there, and you didn't need to be. Headlands went dark at night the way they should, and ships stopped steering for lights where no lighthouse stood.

steps.text: Another ship lost on a calm night, Bale. The third this season. You read weather better than anyone in the Reach. Tell me it was weather.
And Bale? Bring cotton next time you come. The widows sew sails for a living, and they've no cloth.
Bring 20 Cotton Bales to Coralhaven for the sailmakers.
Get your trade moving so you can afford to look into it: reach a net worth of 6,000.
Reach a net worth of 10,000.
Talk to the families of the lost crews in {p1}.
My sister's boy was on the last one. He swam ashore. He says they steered for a light on the point, steady as a lighthouse. There's no lighthouse on that point.
Hire boats to watch the coast at night: raise 10,000 in cash.
Your watch boats saw a red lantern on a bare headland, and a sloop carrying it away before dawn.
Keep the watch boats paid: reach a net worth of 14,000.
You've been drawing on my maps, Bale. Every wreck marked in red.
steps.ok: All on clear nights. All below a headland. All where a lighthouse would be, if you didn't know the coast.

steps.text: Kell's boats know you're asking. Win a fight against them.
The curio dealer in {p2} sells old charts. If anyone has the coast as it used to be, it's that magpie.
steps.ok: Then I'll go and see the magpie.

steps.text: The dealer in {p2} trades charts for spice. Bring 10 Spice Chests.
Lanterna, 1688. The light's arc in red ink. That's the year the Morning Star went down, isn't it? You've gone grey, navigator.
There's an old sailor in {p3} who says he was on the Morning Star. Ezra Mott. Nobody believes him, he says so many things.
steps.ok: I'll believe him. I was there.

steps.text: Find Ezra Mott at the tavern in {p3}.
Okoro Bale. The navigator boy. You were the only one sober enough to swim. ... The lamp went out at two bells, steady as you like. No storm. Somebody turned it down.
And Hollis Kell left Lanterna a year later with a new coat and a full purse. I always wondered where a lamp-keeper finds a purse like that.
Wreckers' boats are watching your ship. Win a fight against them.
Win a fight against the wreckers' boats.
Find out where the wrecked cargo is being sold. Ask the merchants of {p4}.
Wreck goods? Crates with the brands scraped off, going cheap. A man called Cassius Kell sells them. His father kept the Lanterna light, years back.
Cassius Kell's father kept the Lanterna light the night the Morning Star went down.
Reach a net worth of 24,000.
Kell's salvage boats work the wrecks after dark. Sink 2 of them.
Red glass and a hood. You could see that from five miles out and swear it was a harbour. That's how they did it.
steps.ok: That's how they're doing it again.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 32,000.
House Vega trades with governors. Complete a contract to show you can too.
House Vega lost a ship on a clear night last month. Call on Marisol Vega in Puerto Ambar.
Okoro Bale. My father would have hired you on the spot. We lost the Clever Gull on a clear night with a full hold. I'll pay for anything that stops this.
steps.ok: I need an Admiralty officer who'll listen.
steps.name: Marisol Vega, House Vega

steps.text: Commander Hale owes me a favour from the Grimmer business. Put up 20,000 for the hunt, and House Vega will match it.
steps.name: Marisol Vega, House Vega

steps.text: Put 20,000 in a bank as your stake in the hunt.
Something else. The Clever Gull was insured with Harrow & Sons. They paid out in a week, without a single question. Insurers never pay in a week.
steps.ok: Unless they already own the salvage.
steps.name: Marisol Vega, House Vega

steps.text: Bankers trust captains with a record. Complete 2 governor contracts.
Ask the banker in {p5} about Harrow & Sons.
Harrow insures the cargo, and a salvage company buys the wreck rights the week after. Same signature on both. The salvage company pays Cassius Kell. Draw your own picture, captain.
steps.ok: They're paid when it sinks, and paid again when it's salvaged.

steps.text: Kell works two headlands, never the same one twice running. One ship can watch one. You need two.
Buy a second ship to watch the second headland.
Keep both ships at sea: reach a net worth of 60,000.
Lantern on the headland above {p6} last night, and a sloop below it. She'll be back tonight.
Reach a net worth of 75,000.
Catch the lantern sloop off {p6}.
The Wick's crew talked: Kell carries the big lamp on a galleon called the False Light, and he only comes out for rich cargo.
Harrow smiled the whole time, didn't he? Men like that smile while they count.
Harrow's money hires raiders. Sink 2 of them.
Edmund Harrow keeps an office at the market in {p7}. Pay him a visit.
Captain Bale. Wreckers, salvage, lanterns. What an imagination. We're a respectable house. Since you're interested in salvage, I can offer you a share in our next recovery. A generous one.
steps.ok: Your next recovery hasn't sunk yet.

steps.text: Harrow will try to outspend you. Reach a net worth of 90,000.
Hale wants to see you work for governors first: complete a contract.
Commander Hale is stationed at {p8}. Bring her the red lantern.
Commander, for my sins. Vega wrote to me. If Kell is lighting false fires, I need him caught with the lamp lit, at sea, in front of witnesses. My ships are too well known. Yours isn't.
steps.name: Commander Ada Hale

steps.text: Kell goes after sugar. Load a full cargo of it and sail the coast like a man who's never heard of wreckers.
steps.name: Commander Ada Hale

steps.text: Load 40 Cane Sugar as bait for Kell's wreckers.
Kell's scouts take the bait. Sink 2 of them so the big ship has to come out.
Kell's scouts are gone. Next time, he'll come himself.
I've sat in every tavern on this coast for twenty years, Okoro, listening. I know which headlands Kell hasn't used yet. There are three. Cover all three.
Sail with three ships to cover Ezra's headlands.
Reach a net worth of 140,000.
Kell went for my convoy last night, Okoro. Not with a lantern. With guns. I think Harrow is frightened.
steps.ok: Frightened men make noise. Noise is easy to follow.
steps.name: Marisol Vega, House Vega

steps.text: Kell's gunboats are hitting convoys. Win 2 fights against them.
Escort governors' cargo through the danger: complete 2 contracts.
A lit lamp needs witnesses who saw one before. The boy who swam ashore in {p1}, will he speak?
steps.name: Commander Ada Hale

steps.text: Ask the barkeep's nephew in {p1} to stand witness.
He'll do it, if you see his mother right. She hasn't worked since the wreck. A cargo of cocoa to sell from her front room would keep her through the winter.
Bring 25 Cocoa Beans to {p1} for the swimmer's mother.
The swimmer will stand witness before Commander Hale.
You asked about Hollis Kell once. He's alive, navigator. He sold me that chart. He lives in a room above my shop and pays his rent in old stories.
steps.ok: Then I'd like to hear one.

steps.text: Reach a net worth of 180,000.
Find Hollis Kell above the curio shop in {p2}.

The Morning Star. I've waited twenty years for someone to ask me properly. A man from Harrow's paid me forty silver to turn the lamp down at two bells. I thought they'd lose a cargo. I didn't think eleven men would drown.
steps.ok: I was one of the ones who didn't.

steps.text: Then write it down, navigator. I'll put my mark on it. My son learned the trade from me, and I'd like it to end with me.
Kell's galleon is well armed. Build a net worth of 220,000 to fit out for the fight.
Sail the coast off {p9} with your hold full of sugar. Kell will come.
My father let the lamp go out the night your ship went down. Drunk, they said. He wasn't drunk. Harrow paid him, and he taught me the trade.
steps.ok: Your father has said so in writing. It ends with you.

steps.text: Cassius Kell is taken, with the lamp lit, in front of witnesses.
Harrow's lawyers are expensive. So are yours. Reach a net worth of 280,000.
Bring Kell, Hollis's confession and Harrow's ledgers to Commander Hale at the governor's house in {p10}.

Kell's in irons, and Harrow & Sons is shut. The insurance money goes back to the families. I'll send word to Lanterna that the Morning Star's navigator found the men who put out the light. You needn't go back.
steps.ok: I never needed to go back. I needed to know.
steps.name: Commander Ada Hale

steps.text: Lanterna needs a new keeper, Okoro, and a keeper needs wages. The town can't pay them. It never could. That's how Harrow bought the last one.
steps.ok: Then the keeper's wages will come from somewhere else.

steps.text: Lanterna will need ships to bring the keeper's oil. Own four ships.
Fund the Lanterna keeper's wages for twenty years: keep 100,000 in a bank.
They'll read the eleven names when they light it. Yours won't be among them. That's the point, isn't it?
Word goes to Lanterna about the Morning Star, with twenty years of a keeper's wages.
